answer: Each identity claims an orchard plot in the spiral ledger, locks 80 credits, and pays a 30 fee. A ridge rule allows one plot per segment under one operator key; the spiral auditor maps each plot to its ridge and voids duplicates, burning bonds. Each epoch the auditor requires a tending record keyed to that plot alone, costing 15 credits of unbatchable work. A thousand fakes lock 80,000, pay 30,000, and sink 15,000 per epoch, while an honest agent pays 110 once and recovers 80 on exit. A rented-plot ring fails: rented plots carry the owner's key, the check exposes it, and the bond burns.
